questions.q: In traditional Filipino architecture, which heavy and durable wood species is most commonly preferred for structural posts and flooring due to its resistance to decay?
questions.n: Yakal is a high-grade timber known for its extreme strength and durability, making it ideal for structural members.

questions.q: Which type of wood seasoning involves placing the timber in a temperature-controlled chamber to accelerate the removal of moisture?
questions.n: Kiln drying is an artificial seasoning method that uses heat and humidity control to dry wood quickly and uniformly.

questions.q: Which wood defect is characterized by a separation of the wood fibers along the annual rings, often caused by heavy winds during the tree's growth?
questions.n: Also known as ring shakes, these are circular splits following the line of annual rings caused by external mechanical stress.

questions.q: What is the primary difference between Thermoplastics and Thermosetting plastics?
o: Thermoplastics are only used for adhesives, while Thermosets are used for pipes.
Thermoplastics can be remelted and reshaped, while Thermosets remain permanent after curing.
Thermosets are made from wood pulp, while Thermoplastics are made from oil.
Thermosets are always transparent, while Thermoplastics are always opaque.
questions.n: Thermosets undergo a chemical change during curing that creates cross-links, preventing them from melting again.

questions.q: In wood framing, which member is a horizontal beam used to support the floor joists or the ends of a structure's floor system?
questions.n: Floor beams (or girders) provide the primary horizontal support for the floor joists and overall floor load.

questions.q: Which adhesive is specifically known for being a water-based glue commonly used for wood-to-wood bonding in the Philippines?
questions.n: Stikwel is a well-known brand of polyvinyl acetate (PVA) glue, which is water-based and ideal for woodworking.

questions.q: Which plastic material is widely used for kitchen laminates (commonly known by the brand name Formica) and belongs to the thermoset group?
questions.n: Melamine resin is a thermoset plastic used to create hard, heat-resistant laminates for furniture and countertops.

questions.q: What is the term for lumber that has been surfaced or planed on at least one side to achieve smooth faces and uniform dimensions?
questions.n: Dressed (or surfaced) lumber has been processed through a planer to create smooth, even surfaces.

questions.q: Which type of wood preservation treatment is usually preferred when the wood will be in contact with the ground or exposed to severe weather?
questions.n: Oil-type preservatives like creosote provide excellent protection against moisture and decay in harsh ground-contact environments.

questions.q: In the context of sustainable Filipino architecture, which material is often used for cladding and is made from woven bamboo splits?
questions.n: Sawali is the traditional woven bamboo matting used for walls and ceilings in Bahay Kubo structures.

questions.q: In wood framing, what is the name of the vertical member that is used to stiffen the wall and provide lateral support between studs?
questions.n: A stud brace (or bridging/blocking) is installed horizontally or diagonally between studs to provide lateral stability and prevent buckling.

questions.q: Which engineered wood product is made by layering thin wood strands in specific orientations and bonding them with wax and resin, often used as an alternative to plywood for sheathing?
questions.n: OSB is characterized by its cross-oriented layers of wood strands, providing high strength and stiffness for structural applications.

questions.q: Which specific wood defect refers to a crack that follows the pith and radiates outward, typically caused by the uneven shrinkage of the heartwood?
questions.n: Heart shakes originate from the center of the tree and spread outward, often found in over-mature timber.

questions.q: In plastic classification, which group does 'Epoxy Resin' and 'Polyurethane' belong to, known for their high heat resistance and inability to be reshaped once set?
questions.n: Thermosetting plastics undergo a permanent chemical reaction (curing) that makes them rigid and heat-stable.

questions.q: What is the recommended thickness for Natural Veneer when applied using contact cement or pneumatic nails for furniture finishes?
questions.n: Standard natural wood veneers used in high-quality carpentry typically fall within this thickness range for durability and ease of application.

questions.q: Which sealant type is highly valued in construction for its excellent UV resistance, flexibility, and long-term durability in outdoor joints?
questions.n: Silicone is inorganic, making it extremely resistant to UV light, temperature extremes, and moisture over many years.

questions.q: In traditional Filipino construction, what material is primarily used for 'Sawali' weaving?
questions.n: Sawali is specifically made from split bamboo poles that are woven into mats for walling and ceilings.

questions.q: Which part of a wood frame sits directly on the foundation and serves as the base for the vertical studs and floor joists?
questions.n: The bed plate or sill plate is the bottom-most horizontal member that anchors the wood frame to the concrete foundation.

questions.q: Which thermoplastic is widely used for high-impact applications like safety helmets and transparent glazing due to its extreme toughness?
questions.n: Polycarbonate is virtually unbreakable and is used for 'bulletproof' glass and protective gear.

questions.q: Which framing system utilizes studs that run continuously from the foundation sill to the roof plate, often requiring long timbers?
questions.n: In balloon framing, vertical studs are continuous through multiple floors, which is now less common due to fire safety concerns.

questions.q: Which specific wood species is historically known in the Philippines as 'Iron Wood' due to its extreme hardness and resistance to marine borers?
questions.n: Molave is exceptionally hard and durable, traditionally used for ship building and railroad ties.

questions.q: Which framing member is placed horizontally to support the ends of rafters at the ridge of a roof?
questions.n: The ridge board serves as the apex connection point for opposing rafters.

questions.q: What is the primary characteristic of 'Dry Rot' in wood?
o: It turns the wood into a liquid-like sludge.
It only occurs in wood with 0% moisture content.
It is caused by extreme exposure to UV sunlight.
It is caused by fungi that can transport water to dry wood.
questions.n: Dry rot fungi use rhizomorphs to carry moisture, allowing them to decay seemingly dry timber.

questions.q: Which type of board is specifically manufactured to be resistant to moisture and is commonly used as a base for wall tiles in bathrooms?
questions.n: Its cement-based composition makes it dimensionally stable and moisture-resistant for wet areas.

questions.q: In adhesive technology, what is the primary use of 'Contact Cement' (commonly known as Rugby in the PH)?
o: Filling large gaps in structural concrete.
Bonding plastic laminates to wood substrates.
questions.n: Contact cement provides an instant, strong bond for large surface areas like countertops.

questions.q: Which thermoset resin is primarily used as the binder in the production of 'Bakelite', the first synthetic plastic?
questions.n: Bakelite is a polyoxybenzylmethylenglycolanhydride, which is a phenolic resin.

questions.q: Which wood framing component is used to support the weight of the structure over an opening, such as a door or window?
questions.n: A header (or lintel) redistributes the load from above to the trimmer studs at the sides of the opening.

questions.q: Which property of sealants refers to the time required for the material to lose its tackiness on the surface?
questions.n: Tack-free time is the specific measurement of when the surface is no longer sticky to the touch.

questions.q: What is the common term for a wood defect where the grain is not parallel to the longitudinal axis of the piece, often leading to warping?
questions.n: Cross grain occurs when the wood fibers deviate from the straight path along the length of the board.

questions.q: Which thermoplastic is known for having the lowest coefficient of friction and is used for gaskets and non-stick applications?
questions.n: PTFE is highly unreactive and incredibly slippery, making it ideal for low-friction mechanical parts.

questions.q: In 'Platform Framing', which member is installed to provide a solid base for the wall studs of the story above?
questions.n: The sole plate (or bottom plate) is nailed directly to the subfloor or floor platform.

questions.q: Which type of plywood is manufactured with waterproof glue (Phenolic) and is specifically intended for external or high-moisture use?
questions.n: Marine plywood uses high-quality veneers and waterproof phenolic resin to resist delamination in wet environments.

questions.q: What is the primary architectural purpose of a 'Green Roof' in the context of sustainable wood construction?
o: To hide the use of cheap wood materials.
To reduce the heat island effect and manage rainwater runoff.
To increase the structural weight to prevent wind uplift.
To provide a natural habitat for wood-boring insects.
questions.n: Green roofs provide thermal insulation and absorb rainwater, protecting the structure from extreme temp shifts.

questions.q: Which adhesive is most suitable for bonding heavy AAC (Autoclaved Aerated Concrete) blocks?
questions.n: This is a thin-bed mortar specially formulated to match the thermal and structural properties of AAC blocks.

questions.q: In wood framing, what is the purpose of a 'Double Top Plate'?
o: To provide a continuous tie along the top of the wall and support rafters or joists.
To provide a surface for nailing the exterior cladding.
To increase the height of the ceiling by exactly 4 inches.
To act as a fire-stop between the wall and the roof.
questions.n: The second plate overlaps joints in the first plate, creating a stronger structural bond across the wall length.

questions.q: Which wood species is commonly used for high-end furniture and is protected under Philippine law as a 'premium' hardwood?
questions.n: Narra is highly regulated and widely considered the finest Philippine wood for cabinetry and furniture.

questions.q: Which type of plastic board is often used as a lightweight, durable alternative for signage and formwork?
questions.n: Polypropylene boards are chemical resistant, lightweight, and tough enough for repeat usage in formworks.

questions.q: What is the result of 'Artificial Seasoning' known as Kiln Drying?
o: Making the wood impossible to saw or nail.
A permanent change in the color of the wood to black.
Reduced weight and increased strength of the wood.
questions.n: Removing excess moisture makes the wood lighter and more dimensionally stable, which often improves effective strength.

questions.q: Which sustainable architecture principle involves collecting and storing water from the roof for later use?
questions.n: This involves gutters, downspouts, and cisterns to reuse water for irrigation or non-potable needs.

questions.q: Which specific wood defect is characterized by a separation of the wood fibers starting from the bark and extending toward the sapwood, usually caused by severe frost or rapid evaporation?
questions.n: Star shakes are wide at the bark and narrow toward the center, often resulting from the exterior drying much faster than the interior.

questions.q: In the Philippines, which timber species is most legally protected and requires a special permit for transport, often referred to as 'The Queen of Philippine Woods'?
questions.n: Narra is the national tree and a premium hardwood with strict DENR regulations regarding its harvesting and transport.

questions.q: Which framing member is used specifically to provide a nailing surface for the ends of the subfloor or to support the wall studs at the bottom of a frame?
questions.n: The sill plate (or bed plate) is the first wood member in contact with the foundation, providing the anchor for the entire frame.

questions.q: When calculating board feet, what is the nominal thickness used for a board that is actually 3/4" thick?
questions.n: Board foot calculations always use the nominal size (the size before surfacing), where any thickness less than 1" is treated as 1".

questions.q: Which type of plastic resin is commonly used to manufacture 'safety' glass (laminated glass) as the interlayer that holds shards together upon impact?
questions.n: PVB is a tough, adhesive resin used specifically as the interlayer in laminated safety glass.

questions.q: In wood deterioration, what is the primary requirement for 'Wet Rot' to thrive that distinguishes it from other types of decay?
o: High and consistent moisture content in the wood.
questions.n: Wet rot requires the wood to be significantly damp (often near saturation) for the fungi to grow.

questions.q: Which structural framing component is a horizontal member that ties the tops of studs together and supports the floor joists of the next level?
questions.n: The top plate (often doubled) serves to provide a continuous tie and a bearing surface for the structure above.

questions.q: Which adhesive is most appropriate for high-strength, waterproof bonding of wood in boat building or exterior structural applications?
questions.n: Resorcinol is a high-strength, waterproof thermosetting adhesive that is darker in color and highly resistant to weather.

questions.q: What is the standard thickness of a piece of wood categorized as a 'Board'?
questions.n: In lumber grading, a 'board' is defined as lumber that is less than 2 inches in nominal thickness.

questions.q: Which thermoplastic is known as 'Acrylic' (brand name Plexiglass) and is used as a lightweight, shatter-resistant alternative to glass?
questions.n: PMMA is the chemical name for acrylic, valued for its clarity and weather resistance.

questions.q: In the Philippines, which extremely hard wood is often used for the 'mordante' (keel) of a boat or for heavy-duty structural 'yakal' substitutes in bridges?
questions.n: Molave is known for its incredible density and resistance to water, making it a primary choice for maritime structural wood.

questions.q: What is the primary function of a 'Vapor Barrier' when used in conjunction with wood flooring or wall systems?
o: To provide a fire-resistant layer within the wall.
To act as a structural adhesive between the floor and the joist.
To prevent moisture from the ground or atmosphere from entering the wood.
To increase the acoustic insulation between floors.
questions.n: Vapor barriers (like polyethylene sheets) prevent moisture migration that could cause wood to swell or rot.

questions.q: Which framing defect involves a board curving along its edge, making it difficult to use as a straight top plate or floor joist?
questions.n: A crook (or crown) is a warp along the edge of the board, which can often be corrected by 'crowning' the joists upward.

questions.q: Which thermoset plastic resin is the primary component in 'Fiberglass' (FRP) used for water tanks and translucent roofing?
questions.n: Unsaturated polyester resin is the most common binder used to saturate glass fibers in FRP production.

questions.q: What is the name of the horizontal member in a roof frame that connects two opposite rafters at a height above the top plate to prevent the rafters from spreading?
questions.n: Collar ties provide tension resistance to prevent the roof from 'spreading' under heavy loads.

questions.q: Which property of a sealant is most critical for joints that undergo significant thermal expansion and contraction, such as those between metal and glass?
questions.n: A sealant must be able to stretch and compress without losing its bond or tearing (cohesive failure).

questions.q: Which engineered board is made by compressing wood fibers under high pressure and heat without the use of much added resin, resulting in a very dense, dark board?
questions.n: Hardboard is made via a 'wet process' where the natural lignin in wood acts as the binder under high pressure.

questions.q: What is the primary difference between 'Heartwood' and 'Sapwood' in terms of structural use?
o: Heartwood is more resistant to decay and insects than sapwood.
Heartwood is the outer layer of the tree.
Sapwood is always stronger than heartwood.
Sapwood is preferred for structural posts.
questions.n: Heartwood contains extractives and tannins that make it more durable; sapwood is the 'living' part that is more prone to rot.

questions.q: Which plastic sealant is 'Hybrid' in nature, combining the paintability of acrylics with the durability of silicones?
questions.n: Hybrid sealants (SMP) are designed to provide the best features of both silicone and polyurethane/acrylic.

questions.q: In traditional Filipino construction, which sustainable material is a fiber from the leafstalk of a plant, used for high-tensile ropes and even woven cladding components?
questions.n: Abaca (Manila Hemp) is world-renowned for its tensile strength and resistance to saltwater, used extensively in PH crafts.

questions.q: Which specific wood defect is a radial crack resulting from the shrinkage of the outer layers of the log, usually occurring during the seasoning process?
questions.n: Checks are seasoning defects that manifest as cracks across the growth rings due to uneven drying.

questions.q: In the context of Philippine timber, which wood species is commonly used for heavy-duty structural members like wharf construction and bridge timbers due to its high density and strength?
questions.n: Guijo is a hardwood valued for its strength and durability in heavy structural and maritime applications.

questions.q: Which structural framing member is a short stud used above a door header or below a window sill to support the framing?
questions.n: Cripple studs fill the space between a header and a top plate or a sill and a bottom plate.

questions.q: Which type of wood preservative is water-soluble and allows the wood to be painted after treatment, commonly used for residential framing?
questions.n: CCA is a water-borne preservative that leaves the wood surface clean and paintable once dry.

questions.q: What is the term for a wood warp where the board curves along its face from end to end, resembling the shape of a boat?
questions.n: A bow is a deviation from flatness along the length of the face of the lumber.

questions.q: Which plastic is a high-performance thermoset often used for electrical components and heavy-duty adhesives because it does not melt when heated?
questions.n: Epoxy is a thermoset that creates strong, heat-resistant bonds and maintains its shape after curing.

questions.q: In wood flooring installation, what is the term for the process of interlocking boards using a protruding ridge on one side and a corresponding recess on the other?
questions.n: Tongue and groove (T&G) joints allow for a tight, flush fit that accommodates natural wood expansion.

questions.q: Which adhesive is specifically recommended for bonding 'laminated' plastic sheets (HPL) to a particleboard or plywood substrate?
questions.n: Contact cement provides the immediate, high-strength surface bond required for thin laminates.

questions.q: Which wood seasoning defect is characterized by the interior of the wood drying much slower than the surface, resulting in internal stresses and cracks that are not visible on the outside?
questions.n: Honeycombing occurs when internal checks form due to the core being 'case-hardened' and shrinking against the dry shell.

questions.q: What is the actual dimension of a nominal 2" x 4" piece of surfaced lumber?
questions.n: Lumber is planed down from its nominal size; for a 2x4, 1/2" is removed from both dimensions.

questions.q: Which framing member is used specifically to support the header over a door or window opening, transferring the load down to the bottom plate?
questions.n: Jack studs are shortened studs that support the header and define the height of the opening.

questions.q: In the Philippines, which wood species is historically preferred for the manufacture of high-quality 'Arnis' sticks and tool handles due to its shock-absorbing density?
questions.n: Kamagong (Philippine Ebony) is an extremely dense, dark wood prized for high-impact tools and luxury items.

questions.q: Which wood seasoning defect results in the wood collapsing or becoming 'corrugated' on the surface because the free water was removed too rapidly from the cells?
questions.n: Collapse is a severe seasoning defect where wood cells flatten, leading to a distorted surface appearance.

questions.q: When calculating the board feet of lumber, what is the correct formula to use?
questions.n: The standard formula uses Thickness (in), Width (in), and Length (ft) divided by 12 to find the volume in board feet.

questions.q: Which adhesive is most suitable for bonding non-porous surfaces like plastic laminates to a countertop, where clamping is not possible?
questions.n: Contact cement creates an immediate bond on contact, making it ideal for large surfaces like laminates.

questions.q: What is the primary difference between a 'Knot' and a 'Pitch Pocket' in wood?
o: A knot is a branch base, while a pitch pocket is a resin-filled opening.
A knot is a seasoning defect, while a pitch pocket is a growth defect.
A pitch pocket is much harder than a knot.
They are the same thing, just different names.
questions.n: Knots are biological growth features of branches; pitch pockets are internal voids containing liquid or solid resin.

questions.q: In structural wood framing, which member is used to span between floor joists to provide lateral stability and distribute concentrated loads?
questions.n: Bridging prevents joists from twisting and helps the floor system act as a single unit.

questions.q: Which thermoplastic is highly resistant to chemicals and is the most common material used for DWV (Drain, Waste, and Vent) piping in the Philippines?
questions.n: uPVC is rigid, durable, and chemically resistant, making it the standard for sanitary piping.

questions.q: Which seasoning defect is characterized by internal cracks that form a 'honeycomb' pattern, caused by the core of the wood drying and shrinking after the surface has already hardened?
questions.n: Honeycombing is a severe internal failure caused by excessive stresses during the kiln-drying process.

questions.q: What is the actual thickness of a nominal 1" thick piece of dressed lumber?
questions.n: Standard dressing (S4S) for 1" nominal lumber results in an actual thickness of 3/4".

questions.q: Which specific wood framing member is used to provide a nailing surface for the ceiling finish and to keep the top plates of the wall aligned?
questions.n: Ceiling joists support the ceiling finish and act as ties for the exterior walls to prevent spreading.

questions.q: In the Philippines, which resin is primarily used in the production of high-pressure laminates (HPL) like Formica to provide a hard, heat-resistant surface?
questions.n: Melamine resin is a thermoset known for its extreme hardness and resistance to heat and chemicals.

questions.q: What is the term for a wood defect caused by a parasitic plant that sends roots into the tree, resulting in small holes surrounded by discolored wood?
questions.n: Bird pecks are caused by birds like woodpeckers, creating small holes that may lead to decay or staining.

questions.q: Which structural member is placed vertically at the sides of a door or window opening and runs continuously from the bottom plate to the top plate?
questions.n: The king stud provides the full-height vertical boundary for an opening in a wall frame.

questions.q: Calculate the board feet (BF) for 10 pieces of 2" x 6" x 14' lumber.
Which type of wood glue is made from the hides and bones of animals and is often used in traditional lutherie (instrument making) because the joints can be reopened with heat?
questions.n: Hide glue is reversible with heat and moisture, making it ideal for repairs in high-end furniture and instruments.

questions.q: What is the actual dimension of a nominal 2" x 10" piece of surfaced lumber?
questions.n: For lumber 8 inches and wider, the actual width is typically 3/4-inch less than the nominal width.

questions.q: Which specific wood species is a local 'Mahogany' substitute in the Philippines, often used for door jambs and cabinetry, but is susceptible to termites if not treated?
questions.n: Tanguile is the most common 'Philippine Mahogany' used for interior joinery and furniture.

questions.q: In plastics, what does the term 'Plastic Memory' refer to?
o: The ability of a plastic to return to its original shape when reheated.
The time it takes for a plastic to degrade in sunlight.
The shelf life of a resin before it cures.
The capacity of a plastic to store electrical charges.
questions.n: Many thermoplastics 'remember' their extruded or molded shape and will return to it if heated above their softening point.

questions.q: Which wood framing member is used as a 'header' for floor joists, running perpendicular to them to create an opening for a stairwell?
questions.n: Trimmer joists support the headers that frame an opening in a floor system.

questions.q: In the construction of a door or window opening, which member is nailed to the king stud to support the header directly?
questions.n: The jack stud is cut to a specific length to support the weight of the header and transfer it to the sole plate.

questions.q: Which wood seasoning defect involves the wood fibers separating along the annual rings, but unlike a shake, it occurs after the tree is cut due to rapid drying of the surface?
questions.n: Checks are cracks that run across the growth rings and are caused by the exterior of the wood drying faster than the interior.

questions.q: When calculating board feet for a project, if you have a board that is 1 1/2 inches thick, what nominal thickness value must you use in the formula?
questions.n: Board foot calculations always use the nominal size (the size before surfacing), and 1 1/2 inches is the actual thickness of a nominal 2-inch board.

questions.q: Which specific type of engineered wood is produced by bonding wood veneers together with the grain of adjacent layers at right angles, specifically designed for high-stress structural applications like long-span headers?
questions.n: CLT consists of layers of dimensional lumber (planks) stacked at right angles and glued, allowing for massive structural panels.

questions.q: In the Philippines, which locally available wood is known for its distinct 'ribbon grain' and is widely used for high-quality veneers and cabinetry despite being softer than Narra?
questions.n: Tanguile is a member of the Philippine Mahogany group and is prized for its consistent grain and workability for interior finishes.

questions.q: Which property of thermoplastics allows them to be manufactured into complex shapes through 'Injection Molding'?
questions.n: Thermoplastics soften and flow when heat is applied, allowing them to take the shape of a mold before cooling and hardening.

questions.q: In the context of the Rule of Flame Spread, which plastic material is known for producing the most toxic smoke (Hydrogen Chloride) when burned, making its use in plenums restricted?
questions.n: PVC contains chlorine, which is released as toxic and corrosive hydrogen chloride gas during combustion.

questions.q: Which structural member in a floor system is doubled up around openings (like for stairs) to support the tail joists?
questions.n: The header joist is placed perpendicular to the common joists to frame the opening and carry the load of the interrupted joists.

questions.q: What is the primary advantage of using 'Pressure-Treated Lumber' over brush-applied preservatives for wood in ground contact?
o: It eliminates the need for seasoning.
It makes the wood completely fireproof.
Deeper penetration of the preservative into the sapwood.
questions.n: The vacuum-pressure process forces preservatives deep into the wood cells, providing much better protection than surface coatings.

questions.q: Which type of wood warp is characterized by the twisting of the board so that the four corners are no longer in the same plane?
questions.n: A 'wind' or 'twist' occurs when the board rotates along its longitudinal axis, often due to uneven grain.

questions.q: Which specific wood species in the Philippines is often called 'Red Lauan' and is the most common material for plywood face veneers and affordable door panels?
questions.n: Tanguile is the preferred red-tinted Lauan for architectural millwork and cabinetry due to its finer grain.

questions.q: Which thermoplastic is the most common choice for 'Signage' and 'Skylights' because it can be easily heat-formed and has higher clarity than glass?
questions.n: Acrylic is the industry standard for clarity and weatherability in transparent plastic applications.

questions.q: In wood framing, what is the term for the horizontal member used to support the ends of rafters at the base of the roof, often sitting atop the wall studs?
questions.n: The top plate serves as the bearing surface for the roof rafters and ties the wall system together.

questions.q: Which adhesive type consists of two parts (a resin and a hardener) and is used for high-strength structural bonding in extreme environments?
questions.n: Epoxies are thermosetting polymers that require a chemical reaction between two components to reach maximum strength.

questions.q: What is the actual thickness of a 'Two-by-Six' (2x6) piece of S4S lumber?
questions.n: For lumber with a nominal thickness of 2 inches, the surfaced (actual) thickness is standardized at 1 1/2 inches.

questions.q: Which wood defect is caused by the death of a branch that becomes encased by the growing trunk, resulting in a dark ring of bark around the branch base?
questions.n: A loose (or 'dead') knot is not integrated with the surrounding wood fibers and can easily fall out, leaving a hole.

questions.q: In the Philippines, which resin-heavy wood is historically used for 'post and beam' construction in damp areas because its natural oils repel water?
questions.n: Apitong's high resin content makes it durable for heavy-duty framing and exterior structural use.

questions.q: Which plastic is used for the manufacturing of 'Teflon', characterized by its extreme resistance to chemicals and heat?
questions.n: PTFE is the technical name for Teflon, known for its low friction and high chemical stability.

questions.q: What is the standard width of a 'Two-by-Eight' (2x8) surfaced board?
questions.n: Lumber with nominal widths from 8 to 12 inches is typically 3/4 inch narrower than the nominal size.

questions.q: Which engineered wood product is made of wood particles, such as chips and shavings, bonded with resin and is often used as a core material for cheap furniture?
questions.n: Particle board is the most economical engineered board, though it has low strength and poor moisture resistance.

questions.q: Which specific wood preservative process involves pulling a vacuum on the wood before injecting chemicals, ensuring maximum penetration?
questions.n: The Full-Cell (Bethell) process leaves the maximum amount of preservative in the wood cells for severe exposure.

questions.q: In roof framing, which member runs diagonally from the ridge to the top plate at the corners of a hipped roof?
questions.n: Hip rafters form the 'hip' or external corner of a roof where two slopes meet.

questions.q: Which thermoset plastic is used to create the hard, durable coating on 'High-Pressure Laminates' (HPL)?
questions.n: Melamine provides the heat and scratch-resistant surface layer for countertops and furniture panels.

questions.q: Which wood seasoning defect refers to a warp where a board is curved across its width (from edge to edge)?
questions.n: Cupping is the most common result of wood drying faster on one face than the other across its width.

questions.q: What is the primary function of 'Plywood Sheathing' when nailed to wall studs in a wood-frame building?
o: To serve as the final exterior finish.
To provide lateral (shear) stability to the structure.
To support the vertical weight of the roof.
questions.n: Sheathing acts as a 'diaphragm' that prevents the wall from racking (tilting) during wind or seismic events.

questions.q: Which property of a sealant allows it to return to its original shape after being stretched or compressed by a joint's movement?
questions.n: High-performance sealants like silicone have high elasticity, allowing them to cycle through expansion and contraction.

questions.q: In the Philippines, which timber is known as 'Philippine Cedar' and is valued for its aromatic scent and natural insect-repellent properties?
questions.n: Kalantas is a genuine cedar-like wood used for cigar boxes and high-quality wardrobes.

questions.q: Which type of wood warp occurs when the grain is 'spiral' or 'interlocked', causing the board to curve along its edge?
questions.n: A crook is a 'side-to-side' curve along the edge of the lumber, often making the board unusable for long plates.

questions.q: When building a wood-frame wall, what is the maximum standard spacing for studs in a load-bearing wall to ensure structural integrity?
questions.n: 16 inches is the most common structural spacing, though 24 inches is sometimes allowed for non-load-bearing or optimized frames.

questions.q: Which specific Philippine wood species is most commonly used for heavy-duty structural members in wharf construction and bridge timbers due to its exceptional toughness and resinous nature?
questions.n: Apitong is highly resinous and durable, making it the standard choice for heavy structural applications and exterior framing.

questions.q: In the context of wood seasoning defects, which term describes a radial crack that occurs during the drying process due to the shrinkage of the outer layers of the log?
questions.n: Checks are radial cracks caused by the outer wood fibers drying and shrinking faster than the interior fibers.

questions.q: Which thermosetting plastic is primarily used as the binder for 'Formica' and other high-pressure laminates to provide a hard, heat-resistant surface?
questions.n: Melamine is a thermoset known for its extreme hardness and heat resistance, making it ideal for countertop surfaces.

questions.q: In wood framing, what is the name of the horizontal member that provides a continuous tie along the top of the wall and supports the roof rafters?
questions.n: The top plate serves as the bearing surface for rafters and ties the vertical wall studs together.

questions.q: Which specific type of sealant is preferred for joints that experience significant movement and high UV exposure, such as those in glass curtain walls?
questions.n: Silicone is highly flexible and exceptionally resistant to UV radiation and weathering, making it the standard for glazing.

questions.q: What is the actual dimension of a nominal 2" x 6" surfaced (S4S) piece of lumber?
questions.n: For 2-inch nominal thickness, the actual is 1 1/2 inches; for 6-inch nominal width, the actual is 5 1/2 inches.

questions.q: Which wood preservation process involves placing the wood in a cylinder and drawing a vacuum before injecting the preservative under pressure?
questions.n: The Full-Cell process uses a vacuum to remove air from the wood cells, allowing them to be completely filled with preservative.

questions.q: Which framing member is used to provide lateral support and prevent the joists from twisting under a load?
questions.n: Bridging (or cross-bridging) connects joists horizontally to distribute loads and prevent rotation.

questions.q: In the Philippines, which locally available wood is known for its distinct 'ribbon grain' and is widely used for high-quality veneers and cabinetry despite being susceptible to termites?
questions.n: Tanguile is a popular 'Philippine Mahogany' known for its beautiful ribbon grain in quarter-sawn boards.

questions.q: Which thermoplastic is known for its extreme toughness and is used as a transparent alternative to glass in high-security applications?
questions.n: Polycarbonate is virtually unbreakable and is used for bullet-resistant 'glass' and safety shields.

questions.q: Which specific wood seasoning defect is characterized by internal cracks that are not visible on the surface, caused by the core of the timber drying and shrinking after the surface has already 'set'?
questions.n: This defect occurs when internal stresses cause the core to pull apart into a cellular pattern while the exterior remains intact.

questions.q: What is the actual dimension of a nominal 2" x 12" piece of surfaced (S4S) lumber?
questions.n: For widths of 8 inches or more, the standard reduction for surfaced lumber is 3/4 of an inch from the nominal width.

questions.q: Which thermoplastic resin is widely used to manufacture 'safety' or 'shatterproof' glass as the adhesive interlayer that holds the glass fragments together upon impact?
questions.n: PVB is chosen for its clarity, adhesion to glass, and toughness, making it the standard interlayer for laminated glass.

questions.q: In wood framing, which member is installed horizontally between studs at mid-height to provide lateral stiffness and act as a fire stop?
questions.n: Blocking (or fire-blocking) serves both to stiffen the wall against buckling and to slow the spread of fire within wall cavities.

questions.q: Which specific wood species in the Philippines is often called 'White Lauan' and is the most common material for affordable plywood face veneers and light interior framing?
questions.n: Almon is the standard 'White Lauan' used extensively in local construction for light-duty interior applications.

questions.q: Which seasoning defect occurs when the 'free water' is removed too rapidly from the wood cells, causing the cell walls to cave in and the surface to look corrugated?
questions.n: Collapse is a physical distortion of the wood's cellular structure caused by high capillary tension during rapid drying.

questions.q: What is the result of 'Empty-Cell' pressure treatment compared to 'Full-Cell' treatment?
o: Lower retention of preservative but deep penetration.
Weakening of the wood's structural fibers.
Higher retention of preservative and deep penetration.
questions.n: The Empty-Cell process uses compressed air to blow excess preservative out of the cells, leaving only a coating on the cell walls.

questions.q: Which framing member is used specifically to support a window sill, transferring its load to the bottom plate?
questions.n: Cripple studs are the short vertical members located below a window sill or above a header.

questions.q: Which property of a plastic sealant refers to its ability to remain effective and maintain its bond when exposed to chemicals, acids, or salts in an industrial environment?
questions.n: Chemical resistance is the specific property that allows sealants to survive in harsh industrial or laboratory settings.

questions.q: Calculate the total board feet (BF) for 20 pieces of 2" x 8" x 16' lumber.
In a standard wood-framed floor system, which member is installed perpendicular to the joists to prevent them from twisting and to help distribute heavy concentrated loads?
questions.n: Bridging consists of small diagonal or horizontal braces that provide lateral stability and load distribution between floor joists.

questions.q: Which engineered wood product is made by bonding large wood flakes with waterproof adhesive under heat and pressure, commonly used as a cost-effective alternative to plywood for wall sheathing?
questions.n: OSB uses rectangular wood strands arranged in layers at right angles, providing high structural strength for sheathing applications.

questions.q: In the Philippines, which type of contact adhesive is historically associated with the brand 'Rugby' and is primarily used for bonding high-pressure laminates to wood substrates?
questions.n: This synthetic rubber base provides the instant 'tack' and flexible bond necessary for applying laminates to countertops.

questions.q: When building a wood-framed wall, what is the vertical member that is shortened to support the weight of the 'header' over a door or window?
questions.n: The jack stud (or trimmer) is nailed to a king stud to provide the actual bearing surface for the ends of the header.

questions.q: Which specific wood defect is a radial crack resulting from the shrinkage of the outer layers of the log, usually occurring during the seasoning process?
questions.n: Checks are shallow cracks across the growth rings caused by the surface of the timber drying faster than the interior.

questions.q: Which plastic material is used to manufacture 'Teflon' coatings and is prized in construction for its chemical inertness and extremely low friction?
questions.n: PTFE is a high-performance thermoplastic used for gaskets, expansion joints, and non-stick architectural coatings.

questions.q: In traditional Filipino construction, which sustainable material is a fiber from the leafstalk of a plant, used for high-tensile ropes and woven cladding components?
questions.n: Abaca, also known as Manila Hemp, is renowned for its strength and resistance to saltwater, making it ideal for structural cordage.

questions.q: Which type of wood warp is characterized by a curve along the 'edge' of the board, making it look like a crescent moon when viewed from above?
questions.n: A crook (or side-bend) occurs along the edge of the timber, unlike a bow which occurs along the wide face.

questions.q: Calculate the board feet (BF) for 12 pieces of 2" x 10" x 14' lumber.
Which framing member is used as a 'header' for floor joists, running perpendicular to them to create a large opening, such as for a stairwell?
questions.n: Trimmer joists are doubled-up members that frame the sides of an opening to support the header and tail joists.
